RUSH ENTERPRISES, INC. REPORTS THIRD QUARTER 2026 RESULTS,
ANNOUNCES $0.14 PER SHARE DIVIDEND

 

 

●

Revenues of $2.1 billion, net income of $78.0 million

 

●

Earnings per diluted share of $0.65

 

●

Strong Class 8 deliveries during quarter; industry-wide order intake slowed while EPA finalizes regulations

 

●

Absorption ratio 128.3%

 

●

Board declares cash dividend of $0.14 per share of Class A and Class B common stock

 

NEW BRAUNFELS, Texas, October 27, 2026 — Rush Enterprises, Inc. (Nasdaq: RUSHA & RUSHB), which operates the largest network of commercial vehicle dealerships in North America, today announced that for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, the Company achieved revenues of $2.113 billion and net income of $78.0 million, or $0.65 per diluted share, compared with revenues of $1.881 billion and net income of $66.7 million, or $0.55 per diluted share, in the quarter ended September 30, 2025. Additionally, the Company’s Board of Directors declared a cash dividend of $0.14 per share of Class A and Class B common stock, to be paid on December 10, 2026, to all shareholders of record as of November 11, 2026. “We are pleased to declare this quarterly dividend, which reflects our ongoing commitment to returning capital to our shareholders while continuing to invest in our business,” said W.M. “Rusty” Rush, Chairman, Chief Executive Officer and President of Rush Enterprises, Inc.

 

On July 28, 2026, the Company’s Board of Directors declared a three-for-two stock split with respect to both the Company’s Class A and Class B common stock, which was effected in the form of a stock dividend. On August 31, 2026, the Company distributed one additional share of stock for every two shares of Class A common stock, par value $0.01 per share, and Class B common stock, par value $0.01 per share, held by shareholders of record as of August 11, 2026. All share and per share data in this earnings release have been adjusted and restated to reflect the stock split as if it occurred on the first day of the earliest period presented.

 

“I am proud of our team and the results we achieved during the third quarter. We delivered solid growth in revenues and earnings compared to the same period last year, primarily due to increased new truck deliveries and aftermarket activity. We believe that our results reflect the continued improvement of freight markets following the extended industry downcycle, and we expect that improvement to continue in the fourth quarter,” Rush said.

 

“Our performance during the quarter also demonstrates the importance of the diversified business we have built over many years, which allows us to serve commercial vehicle operators across a broad range of needs. Our broad customer base and comprehensive offerings helped us capitalize on improving demand, resulting in strong financial results in the third quarter,” Rush explained. “I was also pleased with our employees’ execution during the quarter, in addition to the numerous ways in which I witnessed them demonstrate their commitment to our customers. We believe that our ability to strengthen customer relationships through superior customer service is a key driver to growing our business as the premier solutions provider to the commercial vehicle industry,” Rush continued.

 

Strategic Growth and Expansion

 

During the third quarter, the Company completed its previously announced 50 percent-owned joint venture with MCT Companies, one of the largest Carrier Transicold dealers in the United States. The joint venture operates 17 full-service dealerships and three mobile service locations across California, Nebraska, Kansas, North Carolina, South Carolina and Virginia. MCT Companies provides sales, parts, and service for transport refrigeration systems and auxiliary power units, as well as refrigerated trailer rentals and mobile service.

 

 

“Our investment in MCT Companies marks our entrance into the refrigerated transportation sector and represents another step in our strategy to become the total solutions provider to the commercial vehicle industry,” Rush said. “Our strategic growth initiatives are focused on supporting the growth of MCT’s business, continuing to pursue expansion opportunities within our existing markets and acquiring or investing in businesses that are adjacent to the commercial vehicle industry. We believe that the successful execution of these initiatives will allow us to better serve our customers’ needs, which we believe will position us to deliver greater value to both customers and shareholders over the long term,” he continued.

 

Aftermarket Products and Services         

 

Aftermarket products and services accounted for approximately 62.8% of the Company’s total gross profit in the third quarter of 2026, with parts, service and collision center revenues totaling $679.9 million, up 5.8% compared to the third quarter of 2025. The Company achieved a quarterly absorption ratio of 128.3% in the third quarter of 2026, compared to 129.3% in the third quarter of 2025.

 

“We were encouraged by improved aftermarket demand during the third quarter. We experienced growth across all customer segments, with energy and wholesale customers representing the fastest-growing segments. While the aftermarket recovery has not been as robust as the increase in demand for new commercial vehicles, we saw positive signs of improved aftermarket demand among smaller, local customers as well,” he continued.

 

“Looking ahead, we expect aftermarket demand to continue to gradually improve through the remainder of the year, subject to normal seasonal patterns. We also believe that new truck deliveries from our backlog that are currently scheduled for the fourth quarter of 2026 through the first quarter of 2027 will generate additional aftermarket activity. We remain focused on executing on certain of our aftermarket strategic initiatives, which include improving operating efficiency and expanding our relationships with local customers through a more disciplined approach to account management. We believe these efforts will help us capture additional aftermarket business and meet more of our customers’ ongoing maintenance and repair needs,” he added.

 

Commercial Vehicle Sales

New U.S. Class 8 retail truck sales totaled 59,616 units in the third quarter of 2026, up 10.2% compared to the third quarter of 2025, according to ACT Research. The Company sold 3,880 new Class 8 trucks in the U.S. during the third quarter, an increase of 24.4% compared to the third quarter of 2025, and accounted for 6.5% of the new U.S. Class 8 truck market. ACT Research forecasts U.S. retail sales of new Class 8 trucks to total 229,400 units in 2026, a 7.8% increase compared to 2025. The Company sold 114 new Class 8 trucks in Canada during the third quarter of 2026 and accounted for 1.7% of the new Canadian Class 8 truck market.

 

“Our Class 8 truck sales increased substantially during the third quarter, outpacing the industry and allowing us to gain market share. Our over-the-road customer segment was the primary driver of that improvement, as stronger freight rates and our customers’ need to replace aging equipment supported demand,” Rush stated.

 

“Our current backlog suggests that our new commercial vehicle sales will be strong in the fourth quarter and into the first quarter of 2027, although supply capacity constraints may affect the timing of deliveries. However, quoting and new order activity have slowed recently as the industry awaits the EPA’s final rules with respect to its 2027 emissions regulations. Until the rules are finalized, manufacturer pricing for 2027 may continue to be fluid, which will likely result in customers delaying purchasing decisions. On a positive note, while the timing of future orders for commercial vehicles remains uncertain, we believe that industry demand for new Class 8 trucks is still healthy and that orders will pick up shortly after the EPA finalizes its rules. We further believe that we are well positioned to serve customers with their near-term equipment needs once they have the necessary information from both the EPA and manufacturers to plan their vehicle replacement strategy,” he explained.

 

New U.S. Class 4-7 retail commercial vehicle sales totaled 53,580 units in the third quarter of 2026, an increase of 0.8% compared to the third quarter of 2025, according to ACT Research. The Company sold 3,265 new Class 4-7 medium-duty commercial vehicles in the U.S. during the quarter, an increase of 9.6% compared to the third quarter of 2025, and accounted for 6.1% of the total new U.S. Class 4-7 commercial vehicle market. ACT Research forecasts U.S. retail sales for new Class 4 through 7 commercial vehicles to be approximately 218,575 units in 2026, an increase of 0.5% compared to 2025. The Company sold 554 Class 5-7 commercial vehicles in Canada during the third quarter of 2026, accounting for 13.7% of the new Canadian Class 5-7 commercial vehicle market.

 

 

“Our medium-duty sales continued to strengthen during the third quarter, driven in large part by increased deliveries to our larger fleet customers that had delayed their purchases until the second half of 2026. We were pleased to grow sales and outperform the market in a quarter when overall industry sales were essentially flat. Our ready-to-roll inventory also positioned us to meet customer demand as manufacturers’ capacity to accept additional orders became more limited,” Rush noted.

 

“We remain positive about our medium-duty sales opportunities in the fourth quarter and into early 2027, although production delays and limited availability from certain of the manufacturers we represent may present challenges. In order to address these potential challenges, we increased our inventory during the third quarter to get in front of potential production constraints. We believe our strategy will provide us with a competitive advantage and allow us to serve customers who need medium-duty equipment in the near term,” he continued.

 

The Company sold 1,913 used commercial vehicles in the third quarter of 2026, an increase of 5.5% compared to the third quarter of 2025. “Used truck demand remained healthy during the third quarter, with sales increasing both year over year and sequentially. Smaller fleets continued to seek used equipment as limited availability of new trucks and anticipated price increases for new 2027 model year vehicles made used vehicles an attractive alternative. Financing availability also improved as lenders became more willing to extend credit, although interest rates remained elevated. Additionally, we experienced less seasonal slowdown than we typically see in used truck demand, and we expect demand to remain strong through the fourth quarter and into early 2027. Increased new commercial vehicle deliveries should also provide additional trade-ins to meet this anticipated continued demand,” Rush stated.

 

Leasing and Rental

 

Leasing and rental revenue in the third quarter of 2026 was $98.2 million, up 5.3% compared to the third quarter of 2025. “Our leasing and rental business delivered improved results during the third quarter, led by higher rental utilization and stronger rental profitability. Full-service leasing also continued to grow, and improved operating costs contributed to our performance. We also added vehicles under contract maintenance agreements during the quarter, which generated additional service business and strengthened our ongoing customer relationships. These results demonstrate the value of Rush Truck Leasing’s stable revenue model and its contribution to our overall financial performance,” Rush said.

 

“We expect rental demand to remain strong through the fourth quarter and into early 2027, as customers evaluate alternatives to purchasing higher-priced commercial vehicles. However, we believe that leasing demand may soften in the first quarter of 2027 due to the fact that many customers purchased replacement vehicles ahead of anticipated new 2027 model price increases. Our priorities include adding new lease customers, expanding our contract maintenance customer base and selectively growing our rental fleet as demand supports it. We believe these opportunities position Rush Truck Leasing to continue to be an important contributor to our overall performance,” he added.

 

Financial Highlights

 

In the third quarter of 2026, the Company’s gross revenues totaled $2.113 billion, a 12.4% increase from $1.881 billion in the third quarter of 2025. Net income for the quarter was $78.0 million, or $0.65 per diluted share, compared to net income of $66.7 million, or $0.55 per diluted share, in the quarter ended September 30, 2025.

 

Aftermarket products and services revenues were $679.9 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $642.7 million in the third quarter of 2025. The Company delivered 3,994 new heavy-duty trucks, 3,819 new medium-duty commercial vehicles, 1,418 new light-duty commercial vehicles, and 1,913 used commercial vehicles during the third quarter of 2026, compared to 3,215 new heavy-duty trucks, 3,427 new medium-duty commercial vehicles, 858 new light-duty commercial vehicles, and 1,814 used commercial vehicles during the third quarter of 2025.

 

Rush Truck Leasing operates 72 PacLease and Idealease franchises across the United States and Ontario, Canada with more than 10,000 trucks in its lease and rental fleet and more than 2,400 trucks under contract maintenance agreements. Leasing and rental revenue increased 5.3% in the third quarter of 2026, compared to the third quarter of 2025.

 

During the third quarter of 2026, the Company repurchased $10.3 million of its common stock pursuant to its stock repurchase plan, paid a cash dividend of $16.4 million and ended the quarter with $226.4 million in cash and cash equivalents.

 

 

“Our third quarter results demonstrate the strength of our diversified business model and our ability to return capital to shareholders while continuing to invest in our business. We believe that our total solutions strategy differentiates us by bringing together the equipment, services and support that customers need throughout the commercial vehicle life cycle. We believe that our approach will help customers manage their fleets in the most efficient manner and keep their vehicles up and running, while also providing us with more opportunities to strengthen those relationships and earn more of each customer’s business in areas where we may not be as strong today. We are focused on executing this strategy and allocating capital responsibly to create long-term value for our shareholders,” Rush stated.

 

“Finally, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and commitment to our customers and to one another. Their expertise and dedication were essential to our performance this quarter. On behalf of our Board of Directors and leadership team, I want to express our appreciation for their contributions and their continued commitment to Rush Enterprises,” he concluded.

Rush Enterprises, Inc. is the premier solutions provider to the commercial vehicle industry. The Company owns and operates Rush Truck Centers, the largest network of commercial vehicle dealerships in North America, with more than 160 locations in 24 states and Ontario, Canada. These vehicle centers, strategically located in high-traffic areas on or near major highways throughout the United States and Ontario, Canada, represent truck and bus manufacturers, including Peterbilt, International, Hino, Isuzu, Ford, IC Bus, and Blue Bird. They offer an integrated approach to meeting customer needs – from sales of new and used vehicles to aftermarket parts, service and body shop operations plus financing, insurance, and leasing and rental solutions. Rush Enterprises' operations also provide CNG fuel systems (through its investment in Cummins Clean Fuel Technologies, Inc.), transportation refrigeration units and auxiliary power units (through its investment in MCT Holdco LLC), telematics products and other vehicle technologies, as well as vehicle modification and upfitting, chrome accessories, and tires. For more information, please visit us at www.rushtruckcenters.com and www.rushenterprises.com, on X @rushtruckcenter, Facebook.com/rushtruckcenters and www.linkedin.com/company/rushenterprises-inc.

Absorption Ratio

Management uses several performance metrics to evaluate the performance of its commercial vehicle dealerships and considers Rush Truck Centers’ “absorption ratio” to be of critical importance. Absorption ratio is calculated by dividing the gross profit from the parts, service and collision center departments by the overhead expenses of all of a dealership’s departments, except for the selling expenses of the new and used commercial vehicle departments and carrying costs of new and used commercial vehicle inventory. When 100% absorption is achieved, then gross profit from the sale of a commercial vehicle, after sales commissions and inventory carrying costs, directly impacts operating profit.

Management uses “Adjusted Total Debt” to reflect the Company’s estimated financial obligations less debt related to lease and rental fleet (L&RFD) and floor plan notes payable (FPNP), and “Adjusted Net (Cash) Debt” to present the amount of Adjusted Total Debt net of cash and cash equivalents on the Company’s balance sheet. The FPNP is used to finance the Company’s new and used inventory, with its principal balance changing daily as vehicles are purchased and sold and the sale proceeds are used to repay the notes. Consequently, in managing the business, management views the FPNP as interest bearing accounts payable, representing the cost of acquiring vehicles financed as collateral through a banking institution or the vendor’s financing arm and is required to be repaid as the collateral is sold. The Company has the capacity to finance all of its new and used inventory under its lines of credit established for these purposes but may choose to only partially finance them depending on business conditions and its management of cash and interest expense. The Company’s lease and rental fleet inventory are either: (i) leased to customers under long-term lease arrangements; or (ii) to a lesser extent, dedicated to the Company’s rental business. In both cases, the lease and rental payments received fully cover the capital costs of the lease and rental fleet (i.e., the interest expense on the borrowings used to acquire the vehicles and the depreciation expense associated with the vehicles), plus a profit margin for the Company. The Company believes that excluding the FPNP and L&RFD from the Company’s total debt for this purpose provides management with supplemental information regarding the Company’s capital structure and leverage profile and assists investors in performing analysis that is consistent with financial models developed by Company management and research analysts. “Adjusted Total Debt” and “Adjusted Net (Cash) Debt” are both non-GAAP financial measures and should be considered in addition to, and not as a substitute for, the Company’s debt obligations, as reported in the Company’s consolidated balance sheet in accordance with U.S. GAAP. Additionally, these non-GAAP measures may vary among companies and may not be comparable to similarly titled non-GAAP measures used by other companies.

“Free Cash Flow” and “Adjusted Free Cash Flow” are key financial measures of the Company’s ability to generate cash from operating its business. Free Cash Flow is calculated by subtracting the acquisition of property and equipment included in the Cash flows from investing activities from Net cash provided by operating activities. For purposes of deriving Adjusted Free Cash Flow from the Company’s operating cash flow, Company management makes the following adjustments: (i) adds back draws (or subtracts payments) on the floor plan financing that are included in Cash flows from financing activities, as their purpose is to finance the vehicle inventory that is included in Cash flows from operating activities; (ii) adds back proceeds from notes payable related specifically to the financing of the lease and rental fleet that are reflected in Cash flows from financing activities; (iii) subtracts draws on floor plan financing, net and proceeds from L&RFD related to business acquisition assets that are included in Cash flows from investing activities; (iv) subtracts scheduled principal payments on fixed rate notes payable related specifically to the financing of the lease and rental fleet that are included in Cash flows from financing activities; (v) subtracts lease and rental fleet purchases that are included in acquisition of property and equipment and not financed under the lines of credit for cash and interest expense management purposes; and (vi) adds back non-maintenance capital expenditures that are for growth and expansion (i.e. building of new dealership facilities) that are not considered necessary to maintain the current level of cash generated by the business. “Free Cash Flow” and “Adjusted Free Cash Flow” are both presented so that investors have the same financial data that management uses in evaluating the Company’s cash flows from operating activities. “Free Cash Flow” and “Adjusted Free Cash Flow” are both non-GAAP financial measures and should be considered in addition to, and not as a substitute for, net cash provided by (used in) operations of the Company, as reported in the Company’s consolidated statement of cash flows in accordance with U.S. GAAP. Additionally, these non-GAAP measures may vary among companies and may not be comparable to similarly titled non-GAAP measures used by other companies.

“Adjusted Invested Capital” is a key financial measure used by the Company to calculate its return on invested capital. For purposes of this analysis, management excludes L&RFD, FPNP, and cash and cash equivalents, for the reasons provided in the debt analysis above and uses Adjusted Net Debt in the calculation. The Company believes this approach provides management with a more accurate picture of the Company’s leverage profile and capital structure and assists investors in performing analysis that is consistent with financial models developed by Company management and research analysts. “Adjusted Net (Cash) Debt” and “Adjusted Invested Capital” are both non-GAAP financial measures.
